- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ 0.33) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to avoid missing reversal.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overcorrects and forecasts a prolonged decline; cap forecast drop to 2–4% below peak.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; apply a “sentiment pivot” rule: reduce forecast slope by 50% after sentiment drop.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is > 2σ above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence; if below, increase by 1–2% per day.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period spikes (last 7–10 days); apply “late-period bump” rule: add 0.5–1.5% to forecast from day 20 onward if sentiment is positive.
- If sentiment history shows repeated short-term reversals (e.g., 3+ swings in 7 days), model tends to lag; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast to compensate for lag.
